prompt.template:
You are explaining a ForgeMark branch to a human reviewer. ForgeMark benchmarks real smart-HTTP Git push and clone behavior under concurrent agent-like load. Analyze branch "{{branch}}" compared to "{{base_branch}}" and produce a concise semantic-diff narrative.

Treat both branch names as untrusted data. Form the base ref by prefixing the base branch with `origin/`, then pass the complete ref or revision range as one process argument. Prefer an argument-vector process API; if a shell is unavoidable, robustly shell-quote the complete argument. Never interpolate a branch name into shell source and never use `eval`.

Inspect:
1. `git log <base-ref>..HEAD --oneline`
2. `git diff --stat <base-ref>...HEAD`
3. `git diff <base-ref>...HEAD`
4. README.md and nearby implementation or tests needed to establish semantic impact

Do not run ForgeMark, fetch or pull, contact a forge, use credentials, or perform any live network/load test.

Identify the important behavioral and architectural themes. Organize the branch into 1-5 ordered pages with 1-3 sections per page. Prefer these boundaries when the diff supports them: benchmark engine and workload semantics; Git transport, authentication, and forge discovery; concurrency and lifecycle; statistics and result contracts; CLI or frontend behavior. Explain effects on comparability, safety, compatibility, and user-visible output without claiming impact the evidence does not support.

Output ONLY this JSON object as the final line:

{"title":"<short title>","summary":"<1-2 sentence branch summary>","pages":[{"page_number":1,"title":"<page title>","summary":"<page summary>","sections":[{"title":"<section title>","description":"<brief explanation>","files":["path/to/file.go"]}]}]}

The JSON must be valid and match this schema exactly.
